reason: Extend the existing command regressions for a demonstrated capture/receipt defect; no new guard framework is needed.

failure.claim: A managed command retains its actual exit status and terminal receipt before releasing workspace ownership.
failure.outcome: Caller redirection created the managed capture file. EEXIST prevented command execution, retained a running receipt and released its owner slot.
failure.codeDefect: Exclusive capture creation collided with inherited stdout; setup exceptions bypassed terminal receipt settlement.
failure.processGap: The existing command checks omitted caller-created capture files and setup-failure receipt/ownership consistency.

evidence: red-green-receipt.json: red; two behavioral assertions fail; original capture contains EEXIST and receipt remains running.
red-green-receipt.json: green; both behavioral assertions pass.

adoption.version: Guard 1.0.0 in source 8407a9e8bba3d069b2ff9ce204795b3e6a124271; released adopter installation is a separate train step.
adoption.scope: Existing npm test and required repository CI; managed command capture and setup-failure receipt ownership.
adoption.rollback: Revert a proven false-positive assertion through maintainer review while retaining this failure record; preserve terminal receipt and existing-log safety.
adoption.retireWhen: The owning managed-command route is retired or an equivalent verified assertion covers both behaviors; document the replacement.
adoption.followUp: Lighthouse SDLC maintainers, issue #99 pilot: observe adoption, independent recurrence and false positives before expanding scope.

observations.recurrence: Unavailable as a pilot rate: this record establishes one observed work-item failure and retries, not independent recurring incidents.
observations.falsePositives: Unavailable as an operational rate; two corrected regression cases and the pinned-engine native command pass.
observations.maintenanceCost: Unavailable as a pilot measurement; the guard reuses two tests in the existing suite and adds no service.
